Query Redshift as the signed-in user

Source: R/backend__redshift.R
oauth_db_redshift.Rd

Query Redshift with a visitor's own access using DBI or dbplyr. This helper connects through Redshift's IAM Identity Center integration.

Usage

oauth_db_redshift(
  authorization,
  server,
  database,
  ...,
  driver = "Amazon Redshift (x64)",
  port = 5439L,
  token_type = c("EXT_JWT", "ACCESS_TOKEN"),
  target = NULL,
  required_scopes = character(),
  min_valid_for = 60,
  session = shiny::getDefaultReactiveDomain()
)

Arguments

authorization

auth$connection from a shinyOAuth server module, without parentheses. To select a saved authorization, pass a function that calls auth$connection(id).

server

Database hostname.

database

Database name.

...

Named Redshift ODBC options, such as CaFile or LoginTimeout. The helper sets authentication and verified TLS.

driver

Installed ODBC driver name.

port

Database port.

token_type

"EXT_JWT" for an external provider's JWT access token, or "ACCESS_TOKEN" for an IAM Identity Center access token.

target

Token target name in the shinyOAuth client. NULL uses its default token, including for clients without named targets.

required_scopes

Additional permissions to check before use. Request consent and set the client's permission requirements in shinyOAuth.

min_valid_for

Minimum remaining token lifetime, in seconds, when obtaining a token. Use 0 to accept any unexpired token.

session

Shiny session. Inferred when the helper is created in server().

Value

A reactive function returning an odbc DBI connection.

Details

Install odbc and the AWS Redshift ODBC 2.x driver with IdpTokenAuthPlugin support. The deployment must trust your app's sign-in provider and map users to database permissions. Configure a shinyOAuth client for that provider and the required token audience.

Create con inside server() and call it before querying in a render or reactive expression.

Connection lifetime

Connections open on first use and close on authorization changes, sign-out, or session end. Ordinary token refresh preserves an established SQL connection; a new connection obtains a current token.

Authentication options

The helper passes the token to the driver's IdpTokenAuthPlugin. Use one of the two token_type values above. Identity-enhanced IAM credentials and SUBJECT_TOKEN use separate authentication flows.

See also

oauth_db_microsoft_client(). vignette("redshift", package = "shinyOAuthDB") has sign-in setup and a complete app.

Other database connections: oauth_db_azure_postgres(), oauth_db_azure_sql(), oauth_db_databricks(), oauth_db_duckdb(), oauth_db_fabric_sql(), oauth_db_hana(), oauth_db_oracle(), oauth_db_postgres(), oauth_db_snowflake(), oauth_db_sql_server(), oauth_db_starrocks(), oauth_db_trino()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
con <- oauth_db_redshift(
  auth$connection,
  server = "cluster.example.eu-west-1.redshift.amazonaws.com",
  database = "reporting",
  token_type = "EXT_JWT"
)
output$rows <- shiny::renderTable({
  connection <- con()
  DBI::dbGetQuery(connection, "SELECT current_user")
})
} # }
